title: Report inappropriate reviews on your Business Profile - Google Business Profile Help

facts.fact: Only reviews that violate Google policies are eligible for removal after being reported on a Business Profile.
facts.quote: You can report any review, but only those that violate Google policies are eligible for removal.

facts.fact: Flagged reviews that violate Google's content policies are removed and no longer show on Maps and Search.
facts.quote: Flagged reviews that violate our content policies are removed and will no longer show on Maps and Search.

facts.fact: Google states that businesses should not report a review merely because they disagree with it or dislike it, and that Google does not get involved in conflicts between businesses and customers.
facts.quote: Do not report a review just because you disagree with it or dislike it. Google doesn’t get involved in conflict between businesses and customers.

facts.fact: Review evaluation of a report typically takes several days, according to Google.
facts.quote: Review evaluation typically takes several days.

facts.fact: Reports flagged in the Reviews Management Tool can have the status 'Decision pending', 'Report reviewed – no policy violation', or 'Escalated – check your email for updates'.
facts.quote: **Decision pending:** The review is flagged, but it hasn't been evaluated yet.

facts.fact: A business can select up to 10 reviews at once when submitting a one-time appeal.
facts.quote: You can select up to 10 reviews.

facts.fact: Google allows a one-time appeal when a flagged review does not qualify for removal.
facts.quote: If a flagged review doesn’t qualify for removal, submit a one-time appeal.

facts.fact: Merchants in the EEA can report third-party reviews directly on Google.
facts.quote: Merchants in the EEA can report third-party reviews directly on Google.

facts.fact: Example reasons offered when flagging a review include 'Spam' and 'Profanity'.
